body:
## Purpose / authorization boundary

**Owner direction (2026-10-14):** continue Vellistry implementation using **Codex** as the primary implementation agent, as recorded in owner-selected [ADR-0008 / draft PR #66](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/66). **This issue authorizes a bounded code review/correction/verification handoff to Codex; it does NOT authorize applying remote database migrations, creating cloud users/fixtures, using secret keys or real manuscripts, deployment, paid model calls, or merging PRs.**

**Task:** VEL-IMP-001B / proposed new task identity `VEL-TASK-0005` (verify unused before committing). This is **not IMP-002 chapters**, and is not a resumption of the paused [PR #59](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/59).

## Pinned facts / entry state (re-verify, don't infer)

- Merged `main` as inspected: `4b3996ef7cda878e1af3d679454bd1bb873a79c2` (merged [PR #64](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/64): Library source, 66 focused tests).
- [PR #65](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/65) is a **draft ChatGPT-authored** hosted-Supabase preflight proposal, branch `feat/vel-imp-001b-hosted-cloud-preflight`, inspected head `604e1ebfd0baab930ee4dc39aecf7289dc64188a`. It contains 10 changed files, 11 new synthetic tests, per-app `.env.example` templates, read-only Node preflight, CI wiring and hosted acceptance checklist. Its five PR workflows were verified green as of task writing. **It is not Codex-produced code**.
- [PR #66](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/66) (ADR-0008) is a separate draft documentation PR; as inspected `main` does not yet contain ADR-0008. Initial CI jobs on #66 failed without exposed step summaries; failure cause not established. Do not assume it merged.
- Supabase **Cloud** (not self-hosted) dev project `vellistry-dev`, ref `lflkcrnriitrbclangyr`, eu-west-2. Read-only checks found healthy project, **zero public app tables, zero applied migrations**. The two Git SQL migrations remain unapplied to cloud.
- Current *source* and *tests*, not a chat recap, are the primary implementation evidence.

## Codex task — Phase A: repository-only, allowed immediately

1. Check out the **actual** current Git state, preserve existing local work. Read in order: `PROJECT-CONSTITUTION.md`, `SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md`, the latest `CURRENT-STATE.md` section, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/decisions/ADR-0006-...`, [ADR-0008 proposal in PR #66](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/66), accepted MVP scope, `docs/plans/VEL-PLAN-02-ARCHITECTURE-DATA-CONTRACTS-2026-10-11.md`, `docs/plans/VEL-PLAN-04-TEST-SECURITY-RECOVERY-2026-10-11.md`, IMP-001 [execution report](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/blob/main/docs/reports/VEL-IMP-001-LIBRARY-ISOLATION-2026-10-11.md), and current PR #65 diff/plan. If Codex Cloud cannot read private GitHub PR metadata, use a **locally fetched branch comparison** and source files; do not guess.
2. Independently review every changed file in PR #65 and its exact base/head; check that Node 24 `parseEnv` works, per-app env loading matches actual Next/Nest runtime, output never leaks credentials, project URL/key/loopback guard semantics are safe, CI executes the right tests, README/plan does not mislead, and no new migrations/dependencies were slipped in. Verify exact applicability on Windows PowerShell without overwriting ignored local env files.
3. Run **actual checks** in a safe local/CI checkout with no credentials: `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `corepack pnpm test:hosted-preflight`, `corepack pnpm test:library-isolation`, `corepack pnpm check`, `corepack pnpm build`, and `python scripts/agent_workflow.py validate` where available. Also check against new expected tests: absent env should fail safely, public key mismatch rejected, wrong project rejected, local URL rejected, leaked secret never printed. Record exit status; do not invent PASS.
4. Correct only **demonstrated** defects within preflight scope, preferably on the existing #65 PR branch **only when the owner explicitly authorizes Codex to take over that branch**. Otherwise prepare a separate branch based on fresh `main` and transparently identify reused/cherry-picked ChatGPT commits. Do not reattribute earlier commits/tests to Codex.
5. Prepare a **read-only security and migration review** for exactly these checked-in migrations, including privilege/RLS review, cloud-target identity, prerequisites, verification queries, auditable migration-history method, rollback limitations, and explicit migration-authorization hold point:
   - `supabase/migrations/20261009000000_initial_author_books.sql`
   - `supabase/migrations/20261009010000_restrict_accepted_manuscript_dml.sql`
   Do not run these or any DB writes to cloud. Do not run existing K2B scripts against cloud (some intentionally revoke grants and break APIs).
6. Document the exact next acceptance matrix for **future, separately authorized** cloud tests: two disposable Auth users; A creates, refreshes, reopens; B cannot see/read/create as A; forged `owner_id` denied; 401/error/account switching; direct PostgREST old signed-out JWT risk observed and honestly blocked; no private manuscript content or service keys in evidence.

## Scope / explicit exclusions

**Allowed:** read, analyze, add targeted synthetic tests/fixes, document review findings, run safe repo tests and builds, create a draft PR or update an owner-authorized existing task branch, prepare proposed ContextPack/ExecutionBundle and migration plan.

**Not allowed:** any Supabase `apply_migration`, `execute_sql` writes, `db push`, `db reset --linked`, cloud Auth user creation/cleanup, remote fixture writes, live provider calls, schema changes, changing active owner decisions, merging PRs, deployment, or creating a 'production-ready' security claim. The historical logged-out-but-valid JWT / direct PostgREST risk remains a private pilot blocker.

**Branch isolation:** one Codex task, one isolated worktree/branch, pin input SHA. Do not collide with #65/#66 unless owner gives a concrete branch ownership decision. Check uncommitted local work first.

## Evidence/exit conditions

- Report **FACT / INTERPRETATION / PROPOSAL** and exact Codex model/runner, base and head SHAs, changed paths, command outputs with exit codes, CI links on exact head, redacted sensitive evidence, negative test results with `PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED|NOT_RUN`, any unresolved blockers, and owner decision required.
- If no correction is necessary, report **REVIEWED / NO CODE CHANGE REQUIRED**; do not fabricate commits for productivity.
- A proposed ContextPack / ExecutionBundle must follow actual repo validation contracts and unique IDs (do not reuse historical VEL-TASK/VEL-CP/VEL-EB IDs).
- Owner must explicitly review/merge #65 and #66; no assumed approvals.
- Stop before Phase B. **Phase B (cloud migrations, synthetic users and real end-to-end book persistence)** needs separate exact-project scope and owner authorization.

## Codex task launch instruction (copy into a Codex coding session)

> Work in Ben-001-sys/Vellistry as Codex, primary implementation agent. Execute the bounded **repository-only Phase A** of this GitHub issue. First verify current main, draft PR #65/#66 and governing sources; independently inspect #65 and its 11 synthetic tests. Make only evidence-driven, safe corrections; run all feasible no-secret checks with true exits; produce a factual ExecutionBundle and reviewed cloud migration plan. Preserve PR authorship, never touch hosted Supabase data, never merge/deploy/use secrets, and mark cloud acceptance BLOCKED pending separate owner approval. If you cannot access GitHub issue metadata, use the full text of this task supplied by the owner and compare fetched repository branches; state the limitation.
title: VEL-IMP-001B — Codex review, verify and finish hosted Supabase preflight (no cloud writes)
